Yes — the closest match is a debiasing-unlearning approach that removes the influence of specific problematic data points without full retraining. FUDLR reframes fairness debiasing in LLM-based recommender systems as an efficient machine unlearning task, identifying bias-inducing samples and then estimating and removing their influence on model parameters instead of retraining the whole model [2]. CRAGRU is similar in spirit for recommendation unlearning: it targets a user’s data, reduces collateral impact on others, and avoids retraining the base model by using retrieval and generation stages [1].

If you mean search-query suggestion engines specifically, none of the supplied papers directly studies that setting; the closest search-related paper only audits query suggestion bias, not removing data-point influence without full model updates [9].
